comments.body:
## Phase 1 RCA (rebar-debug) — PROVEN, cited; disposition ESCALATE (no code changed)

**Proven root cause.** `_reads._tracker()` (`src/rebar/_reads.py:42`) uses `if not
os.path.isdir(tracker)` as its SOLE initialization predicate. A directory that exists but is
not a usable store satisfies `isdir`, so the guard never fires and the read proceeds; one layer
down the reducer's `except OSError: return results` swallows the failure and yields `[]`. The
caller cannot tell "empty store" from "broken store".

**Runtime confirmation (this worktree, off origin/main `dddaa60`).** Drove the real
`rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=…)` entry point:
- Case 1 (production shape) — tracker dir with a `reviewbot-ensure-tickets` marker file and NO
  `.git`: returned `[]` (should raise `store_uninitialized`).
- Case 3 (mid-clone) — `.git` present but HEAD unresolvable (`git rev-parse --verify HEAD` rc
  128): returned `[]` (should raise `store_uninitialized`).
- Control — an `init_repo` store (has `.git` + resolvable HEAD, zero tickets) reads `[]`
  correctly, and must keep doing so (`tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`).

**Why it is a defect (cited authority).**
- The write side already guards usability: `event_prepare._ensure_initialized`
  (`src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py:101`) raises when `not isdir(tracker) or not
  exists(tracker/.git)`. Reads check only `isdir`, so read/write disagree about the same store.
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` forbids fallback-masking (faults must surface as errors, not resolve
  to a silent fallback); a broken store reading `[]` is exactly that.
- The existing contract test pins the distinction ("directory does not exist" = error vs
  "exists and holds no tickets" = `[]`).
- Standing intent is documented by prior closed tickets: `antelopine-limivorous-chinchilla`
  (introduced the guard + the `store_uninitialized` code), `fathomable-yester-thrip` (recorded
  this as a residual), and `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` AC3 ("while the clone is in flight,
  tracker reads report `store_uninitialized` rather than `[]`" — explicitly left unticked,
  pointing here).

**Defect origin / `caused_by`.** Attributed to `44fd-230c-5893-4246`
(`antelopine-limivorous-chinchilla`), introducing commit `84fc5f9b68df8` (the line
`if not os.path.isdir(tracker):`). That change added the read guard but keyed it on directory
presence only, not store usability — an incomplete implementation of the guard's own intent
(and of parity with the write side, which already checked `.git`). `caused_by` link recorded.
Class if closed: `plan_defect` / incomplete-implementation.

**Caller-dependency gate.** Only consumer of the `store_uninitialized` code is
`rebar.audit.server._audited_tickets` (`src/rebar/audit/server.py:99-102`), which catches that
code and degrades to an empty index while propagating every OTHER error. Extending the guard to
emit `store_uninitialized` for broken/mid-clone stores keeps that caller consistent (it degrades
rather than 500s). No high-confidence behavioral-dependency caller relies on the current `[]`.

**Why ESCALATE rather than auto-land.** This is a genuine defect with documented standing
intent, but the correct fix is NOT behavior-preserving and carries a design choice, so under the
orchestrator's escalation rules it needs human authorization:
1. It changes observable read semantics **repo-wide** — all 7 library/MCP read entry points that
   funnel through `_tracker()` now raise for a class of inputs that previously returned `[]`.
   The ticket itself flags this blast radius as the reason it was scoped out of change 2244.
2. The "usable store" predicate is a design tradeoff: `.env-id` is git-ignored LOCAL state
   (absent immediately after a valid clone — would misclassify a fresh valid clone as
   uninitialized; cf. `ab61-f3e8-6ee6-4905`), so the read-side discriminator should be a
   **resolvable git HEAD** (matches AC3 and the mid-clone case), which adds a HEAD-resolution on
   the read hot path and raises the question of unifying with the write-side check.

**Recommended fix (for the authorizing human).** In `_reads._tracker()`, after the `isdir`
check, also treat the store as uninitialized (same `store_uninitialized` code + wording) when it
is not a usable store — i.e. `.git` absent OR HEAD not resolvable (`git rev-parse --verify -q
HEAD`). Keep the existing empty-initialized-store contract test passing unmodified, add regression
coverage for (a) present dir without `.git`, (b) `.git` present but HEAD unresolvable (mid-clone),
and (c) a guard that fails if the predicate reverts to bare `os.path.isdir`. Consider factoring the
usability predicate so read and write sides share it.

comments.body:
## Fix-plan detail (moved out of the description to keep it under the P4 admission limit)

**Three init gates, precisely.** `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` (a `.git`-presence check on
the low-level append path); `_seam.append_event` at `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:555` (the
AUTHORITATIVE write-command gate, requires `.env-id`; bug roar-nurse-stomp / ab61; pinned by
`tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py`); and the read chokepoint `_reads._tracker`. The one
message string is emitted from ~14 sites enforcing two different preconditions, so read and write
do NOT fully agree by design.

**Why reads deliberately do NOT require `.env-id`.** `.env-id` is git-ignored LOCAL provenance
state, absent immediately after a valid clone. Verified in-session: a store with `.git` + a
resolvable HEAD but no `.env-id` reads its tickets fine, while a write is correctly rejected by
the `_seam` `.env-id` gate. So a just-cloned store MUST stay readable; only writes require the
provenance stamp. The fix therefore closes the `.git`/HEAD read/write disagreement (broken /
mid-clone store readable-as-empty) and intentionally leaves the `.env-id` asymmetry alone.

**Write-gate behavior change + safety (addresses plan-review BLOCK rev2).** Sharing the `.git`+HEAD
predicate means `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` now also rejects a `.git`-present-but-HEAD-
unresolvable (mid-clone) store. Proven safe for the init/first-write path: instrumenting the call
showed `_ensure_initialized` is invoked exactly once across `init_repo` + first `create_ticket`,
and at that call HEAD already resolves -- init creates the store's initial commits through
`init_core`, not through the guarded append path. The full write suite is re-run at GREEN to
confirm no other write path appends into an unborn-HEAD store.

**Pre-mortem (how could this fail?).** (1) init writes before the first commit -> RULED OUT
(single `_ensure_initialized` call, HEAD resolves). (2) another write path appends to an
unborn-HEAD store -> guarded by re-running the full write suite at GREEN. (3) `git` binary absent
-> the predicate's `subprocess.run` uses `check=False`; a nonzero rc means "HEAD not resolvable"
(not usable), while an OSError (git missing) is a distinct environment failure that propagates
rather than masquerading as `store_uninitialized`; covered by a test. (4) perf: `git rev-parse`
per read is negligible -- the read path ALREADY spawns git (throttled `git fetch`/reconverge via
`_fresh`), so no new process class. (5) walk-up false positive -> the explicit `.git`-exists check
precedes the HEAD probe.

**Prior art.** git invoked via `git -C tracker rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, matching the existing
`footprint._git` read-probe pattern; the heavier `gitutil.run_git` is deliberately not reused so
the read chokepoint does not import the write-core lock machinery and `_reads` stays out of the
import SCC.

comments.body:
## Plan-review rev4 (LLM tier ran) — BLOCK on one G6 finding; resolved in rev5 plan

**Blocking (G6).** "Widening `store_uninitialized` to fire for broken/mid-clone stores collides
with the audit-server consumer, which degrades that exact code to an empty page — silently
blanking a genuinely broken store, the same masking this change exists to remove." Cites
`src/rebar/audit/server.py:101` and `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py:163`.

**Analysis.** Correct catch. `audit.server._audited_tickets` catches `store_uninitialized` and
degrades to an empty index. Its docstring PROMISES "a genuinely broken store is not silently
blanked" — a promise that held only because broken/mid-clone stores used to read `[]` (never
raised). This fix makes them raise `store_uninitialized`, so they now fall into the caught bucket
and the docstring's guarantee becomes false. (Behavior at the audit layer is actually unchanged —
those stores rendered empty before too — but the module now silently blanks them while claiming it
does not.)

**Resolution (in approved scope — this is the caller-sweep reconciliation the operator asked me to
complete; NOT a new behavior change).** Keep the index rendering empty for any `store_uninitialized`
(a read-only web index must not 500), but make it HONEST and NON-silent: correct the docstring, and
broaden the WARNING log so a present-but-unusable store is logged. Operators diagnose store health
via the driving agent / CLI, which now surfaces the absent-vs-unusable distinction. Added
`src/rebar/audit/server.py` to file_impact and an AUDIT acceptance criterion (renders empty AND
logs for a present-but-unusable store; still propagates a non-`store_uninitialized` failure).

**Advisory folded in (T5b).** `store_is_usable`'s git-subprocess failure taxonomy is now explicit:
`check=False` so a clean non-zero rc == "HEAD unresolvable" -> not usable, while an OSError (git
binary missing / env failure) PROPAGATES rather than collapsing into `store_uninitialized`. Pinned
by a new predicate test.

Description trimmed to <8000 chars (P4). Re-running `review-plan` for a non-BLOCK verdict.

comments.body:
## Phase 2 (Repair) — implemented per the approved plan; RED→GREEN + mutation-verified

Worktree `../aefe-store-usability` off `origin/main` `565e1856bc9d`. Plan-review attestation
re-checked at implementation time and still `certified` (`review-plan --status`:
`verified_at_sha 565e1856…`, `currency_basis file_impact`).

### RED baseline (drove the real public entry point, not a unit stub)

`rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=…)` against three stores, before any code change:

| store shape | before |
|---|---|
| tracker dir present, `reviewbot-ensure-tickets` marker, NO `.git` (the production shape) | `[]` |
| mid-clone: `.git` present, `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` rc **1** | `[]` |
| control: `init_repo` store, zero tickets | `[]` (correct, must stay) |

Confirms the RCA: all three are indistinguishable. (Minor correction to the Phase-1 note —
the probe returns rc **1**, not 128, because `-q` suppresses the error; non-zero either way,
so the predicate is unaffected.)

### Change (exactly the approved four files + test file)

- **new** `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py` — `store_is_usable(tracker)` = `isdir` AND
  `.git` present AND `git -C <tracker> rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves. Stdlib-only.
  `check=False`, so a clean non-zero rc means "HEAD unresolvable" -> not usable, while an
  `OSError` (git binary missing) PROPAGATES rather than collapsing into a store verdict.
- `src/rebar/_reads.py` — `_tracker` gates on the shared predicate instead of bare `isdir`.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py` — `_ensure_initialized` calls the same predicate
  (the `os` import became unused and was removed).
- `src/rebar/audit/server.py` — docstring corrected to state that EVERY `store_uninitialized`
  (absent AND present-but-unusable) degrades to an empty index, and the WARNING broadened so
  the present-but-unusable case is logged rather than silently blanked. No behaviour change at
  that layer.

46 added lines across the three edited src files + a 56-line new leaf (mostly rationale
comment) — well inside the `bugfix-size-attestation` threshold, and the bug carries a
certified plan-review attestation regardless. One change, no split needed.

### Write-gate safety, proven rather than asserted

Instrumented `_ensure_initialized` across `init_repo` + `create_ticket` + `comment`: **2**
calls, and at BOTH `git rev-parse HEAD` already resolved and `store_is_usable` was `True`.
The probe is anchored — it asserts the guard was actually exercised, so a zero-call run would
fail rather than pass vacuously. Init's initial commits come from `init_core`, not through the
guarded append path, so widening the write gate to reject a mid-clone store does not break
init or first write.

### Mutation results — 6 seeded, 6 killed

Each production edit reverted individually, targeted tests re-run, **return code checked**
(not output eyeballed), and each seed verified to have actually applied (anchored replaces
with `count == 1` asserts; a no-op seed is reported as `SEED-NOOP`, never as a kill).

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `_reads`: `store_is_usable` -> bare `os.path.isdir` | **killed** — 14 failed |
| M2 | write gate: revert to `isdir` + `.git` | **killed** — 1 failed |
| M3 | predicate: drop the `.git` check | **killed** — 8 failed *(see below)* |
| M4 | predicate: drop the HEAD probe (`return True`) | **killed** — 8 failed |
| M5 | predicate: swallow `OSError` as not-usable | **killed** — 1 failed |
| M6 | audit: revert the warning wording | **killed** — 1 failed |

**M3 initially SURVIVED, and that was a real coverage gap, not a mutation-testing artifact.**
`git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD` walks UP to the nearest enclosing repository, so the `.git`-exists
check exists precisely to stop an unusable tracker resolving the enclosing CODE repo's HEAD.
My first fixture built the enclosing repo with `git init` and no commit, so ITS head did not
resolve either — the walk-up hazard was never exercised and deleting the check changed nothing.
Fixed by giving the enclosing repo a real commit (the production shape: the tracker sits inside
a normal checkout) and asserting, as a precondition, that git DOES resolve a HEAD by walking up
from the tracker dir. M3 then fails 8 tests.

### Vacuity anchoring (this bug is literally about vacuous results)

- Every success-asserting test seeds a real ticket and asserts it comes BACK, so `[]` cannot
  satisfy it. The `.env-id` test asserts the seeded id specifically.
- The predicate test asserts `True` for usable shapes as well as `False` for unusable ones, so
  an always-`False` predicate fails it.
- The write-gate test asserts the initialized store is ACCEPTED as well as the mid-clone
  REJECTED, so an always-raising guard fails it.
- The `OSError` test first asserts the store IS usable without the fault injected, so the raise
  is attributable to the injected `OSError` and not to the store's shape.
- **The audit test was itself vacuous on first write and I caught it**: `assert caplog.records`
  passed against the UNFIXED code because it was matching an unrelated
  `REBAR_NO_SYNC`-deprecation warning from `rebar.config`. Now scoped to
  `r.name == "rebar.audit.server"` and to a message naming the unusable case; it fails RED as
  it should.

### Gates

`make lint` rc=0 · `make typecheck` rc=0 (mypy, 685 files) ·
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` `new=0 increased=0` ·
`check_raw_git_writes.py` rc=0 (the probe is a READ verb and carries a `raw-git-ok` marker) ·
target file 30/30 pass. Full `make test` running.

### Discovered work (filed + linked `discovered_from`)

- `contained-coherent-tick` (`fe07-314a-2465-40db`) — the approved plan's out-of-scope parity
  item: `reads_cli.py:340,384` still gate on bare `os.path.isdir`, so the CLI now DISAGREES
  with library/MCP on a broken store (before this fix they agreed, both wrong).
- `gangrene-dissected-nymph` (`d582-e941-96b6-41a8`) — measured, and it contradicts the plan's
  assumption. The plan reasoned the probe is negligible because reads already spawn git; but
  `_fresh` is throttled to <=1/min, so most reads spawn none today and the predicate adds an
  **unthrottled** one. Measured on a 25-ticket store: `list_tickets` 22.7ms with the predicate
  vs 5.6ms with it neutralized — **17.1ms, +305%**. Absolute cost is one git startup and log
  reduction dominates on the production tracker, so I shipped the approved design rather than
  improvise a cache (a cached "usable" verdict is exactly this bug's staleness hazard) or
  hand-roll ref resolution. Recorded for a deliberate decision instead of silently absorbed.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## COLLISION: a parallel session already has this fix — I did NOT push a duplicate change

While preparing to push I found another active session working this same ticket in
`/Users/joeoakhart/fix-rapt-read-semantics`, with commit **`84237944cedb`** ("reads: reject a
present-but-unusable store", `rebar-ticket: aefe-614a-2631-4117`), based on `ae203145fa39` —
the same SHA this ticket's plan-review attestation records as `head_sha`, so that is the
session that earned the attestation.

It is the same design, the same five files, and the same approved plan. **No Gerrit change is
open for this ticket** (`status:open message:aefe-614a` returns nothing; the open list is
2354-2358, none of them this), so their commit is still local — the collision would have
happened at push time.

I therefore **did not push**, to avoid two competing Gerrit changes for one ticket. My work is
committed locally as `9ebaa3490e48` on branch `aefe-store-usability` (off `origin/main`
`565e1856`) if it is ever wanted, but the deliverable below is the part that matters: two
findings their change does not have.

### FINDING 1 — their regression suite does NOT test the check their own commit message calls load-bearing

Their commit message says the `.git`-existence check "precedes the HEAD probe so
`git -C tracker rev-parse` cannot walk up to an enclosing repo and resolve the wrong HEAD",
and their fixture docstring repeats it. But their `_tracker_present_without_git` builds the
enclosing repo with a bare `git init` and **no commit**, so the enclosing HEAD is unborn and
does not resolve either. The walk-up hazard is therefore never exercised, and deleting the
`.git` check changes nothing their tests can see.

**Proven, not inferred.** I copied their test file verbatim and ran it against my source tree
(the two production implementations are equivalent on this point), with and without the
mutation that deletes the `.git`-existence check:

```
BASELINE  (unmutated)              their 28 tests: 28 passed
M3 MUTANT (.git check deleted)     their 28 tests: 28 passed   <-- SURVIVES
M3 MUTANT (.git check deleted)     my tests:        9 failed   <-- killed
```

I hit exactly this hole first and only caught it because the mutation survived. The fix is one
line of fixture: give the enclosing repo a **real commit** (which is also the production shape
— the tracker sits inside a normal checkout) and assert, as a precondition, that
`git -C <tracker> rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` **returns 0** by walking up. Without that
assertion the fixture silently stops testing the thing it exists to test.

A second, smaller one in the same file: their audit assertion
`any(r.levelno >= logging.WARNING for r in caplog.records)` is not scoped to a logger. Mine in
that exact shape **passed against the unfixed code**, matching an unrelated
`REBAR_NO_SYNC`-deprecation warning emitted by `rebar.config`. Scope it to
`r.name == "rebar.audit.server"` (and to a message naming the unusable case) or it can pass for
the wrong reason.

### FINDING 2 — the per-read cost, measured; the plan's assumption is wrong

The approved plan reasoned the probe is negligible "because the read path ALREADY spawns git
(throttled `git fetch`/reconverge via `_fresh`)". `_fresh` is throttled to **at most once per
minute**, so most reads spawn no git today and the predicate adds an **unthrottled** one.
Measured on a 25-ticket store, 40 iterations, `REBAR_NO_SYNC=1`, with only the probe
neutralized:

```
list_tickets WITH predicate:    22.7 ms
list_tickets WITHOUT predicate:  5.6 ms   ->  +17.1 ms, +305%
```

Absolute cost is one git startup and log reduction dominates on the production tracker, so this
is not an argument against the design — but it should be a recorded decision rather than an
unexamined assumption. Filed as `gangrene-dissected-nymph` (`d582-e941-96b6-41a8`,
`discovered_from` this ticket), including why the two obvious optimizations both need a
deliberate call (a cached usability verdict is this bug's own staleness hazard; hand-rolling
ref resolution is fragile across packed-refs / `.git`-as-a-file / detached HEAD).

### Housekeeping

My parity ticket `contained-coherent-tick` (`fe07-314a-2465-40db`) duplicates their
`free-slothful-fennecfox` (`be80-8377-4b4c-44f4`), which is strictly broader — theirs also
covers `descendants.py`, `next_batch.py` and `repo_snapshot.py` beyond `reads_cli.py`. Closing
mine as a duplicate and superseded by theirs.

### Correction to the Phase-1 RCA note

The mid-clone probe returns rc **1**, not 128 — `-q` suppresses the error. Non-zero either way,
so the predicate is unaffected; noting it only so the next reader is not confused by the
citation.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ESCALATION — new design decision beyond approved scope (rebar-debug Phase 2, do NOT force)

The operator-approved predicate `store_is_usable = isdir AND .git present AND
`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves` is implemented and GREEN for its own tests, BUT the
mandated caller-dependency sweep found a SUPPORTED PRODUCTION read path that relies on the old
`[]`-for-`.git`-less-store behavior and is broken by the approved predicate. Resolving it requires
CHANGING the approved predicate, which is a new design decision. Holding here per the rule
"escalate new design decisions; do not force". The change is committed LOCALLY ONLY
(`84237944cedb`) and has NOT been pushed to Gerrit.

== What breaks and why (evidence) ==

`rebar._snapshot.materialize_tickets()` materializes a PINNED, read-only ticket snapshot by
checking a git tree out into `<root>/.tickets-tracker/` via a throwaway index — it creates a
directory of event dirs with NO `.git` (confirmed: repo_snapshot.py `_materialize_tree` /
`materialize_via_donor`; test `test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py::test_materialize_tickets_holds_event_dir`
asserts only `is_dir()` + event dirs, never `.git`). The code-review GATE AGENTS read this pinned
snapshot in production: `LLMConfig.from_env` sets `tickets_path = current_tickets_root()`
(llm/config.py:623) and the agent's rebar ticket tools (`show_ticket`, `list_tickets`, `next_batch`)
resolve the store there — funneling through `_reads._tracker`, the exact chokepoint I widened.

Because a materialized snapshot has no `.git`, `store_is_usable` returns False, so every gate-agent
read now raises `store_uninitialized` instead of reading the pinned store. This is the MCP AGENT
READ SURFACE the approved scope explicitly told me to broaden — it collides with itself.

Reproduced directly: a `.git`-less directory of event files
=> `store_is_usable` = False; `rebar.next_batch(...)` (library/_reads) raises `store_uninitialized`,
while the CLI `next-batch` (a separate read path that does NOT go through `_tracker`) reads it fine.

Failing tests attributable to MY change (6): the 4 `tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py`
pinned/mirror/ref-chain reads, `tests/interfaces/queries/test_next_batch_compute.py::test_library_and_mcp_shape`,
and `tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py::test_stage_and_commit_git_calls_are_all_timeout_bounded`
(the last is separately fixable: my new `rev-parse` subprocess needs a bounded timeout on the write path).
The other 8 full-suite failures (test_atomic_completion_close x5, test_rebar_repo_isolation x1,
test_tracker_footprint_cli x2) FAIL ON CLEAN origin/main too (git `show-ref`/`ls-tree refs/heads/tickets`
=> 128 in this sandbox) — pre-existing/environmental, NOT my change.

== The irreducible conflict ==

The ticket's PRIMARY production incident (#1) is a NO-`.git` directory holding `reviewbot-ensure-tickets`
marker files that must RAISE. A valid materialized snapshot is ALSO a no-`.git` directory that must
READ. They are filesystem-identical except for content: the broken dir has marker files and NO ticket
event dirs; the snapshot has ticket event dirs. So a purely `.git`/HEAD-based predicate CANNOT
distinguish them — it wrongly rejects the snapshot. The approved predicate as written is incompatible
with rebar's supported `.git`-less materialized-snapshot read mode.

== Options (each deviates from the approved predicate — needs operator decision) ==

1. NARROW to the mid-clone case only: `usable = isdir AND (.git present => HEAD resolves)`.
   Raises on mid-clone (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable); ALLOWS every `.git`-less dir (snapshots
   read again). Simple, no heuristic. COST: does NOT fix the ticket's primary incident #1 (no-`.git`
   marker dir still reads `[]`). Materially narrower than approved.

2. ADD materialized-store detection (RECOMMENDED to satisfy the ticket ACs):
   `usable = isdir AND ((.git present AND HEAD resolves) OR (>=1 valid ticket event dir present))`.
   Raises on no-`.git`+no-event-data (incident #1) AND mid-clone; ALLOWS populated snapshots and
   empty INITIALIZED stores (`.git`+HEAD). COST: a new "has event data" heuristic, and an EMPTY
   materialized snapshot (no `.git`, zero tickets) would raise — operator must rule whether that
   edge is acceptable (a gate reading a truly empty ticket store).

3. MODE-GATE: skip the usability guard when a pinned tickets root is active
   (`current_tickets_root() is not None` / resolved tracker == pinned root), keep it for live stores.
   Exempts production snapshots without an event-data heuristic; still fixes incident #1 (live store).
   COST: adds mode-awareness to the read chokepoint, and the library-`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`-at-a-bare-
   event-dir test pattern (`test_next_batch_compute`) would need its store marked pinned or given a
   `.git` — i.e., decide whether that bare-event-dir library read mode is supported in production.

Recommendation: Option 2 (only option that meets the ticket's stated ACs while preserving the
production gate-snapshot read path), with an explicit operator ruling on the empty-snapshot edge;
Option 1 as a narrower fallback if incident #1 coverage is negotiable.

I have NOT implemented any of these (that would be forcing a new design decision). Awaiting operator
direction on which predicate to adopt. The local commit stays unpushed until then.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## STOP — the approved predicate BREAKS the gates. Full-suite evidence: 6 regressions, and one of them is a counter-example to the design

Full suite on my implementation of the approved plan (`pytest -m "not integration and not
external"`, `-n 4 --dist loadfile`, clean run, 29m38s):

```
6 failed, 17843 passed, 61 skipped
```

All six are caused by the change. They split into two causes, and **the first invalidates the
`.git`-presence half of the approved predicate**. The parallel session's commit
(`84237944cedb`) uses the same predicate at the same two call sites, so it will fail
identically — this is not specific to my implementation.

### CAUSE 1 (design-invalidating) — a `.git`-less store is NOT necessarily a broken store: the gate ticket snapshot is one

```
tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py::test_attested_gate_reroots_ticket_tools_to_pinned_store
tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py::test_close_path_pin_sees_writes_made_after_the_mirror_went_stale
tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py::test_fetch_true_pin_loses_nothing_that_origin_holds
tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py::test_falls_back_to_the_ref_chain_when_no_tracker_repo_is_present
tests/interfaces/queries/test_next_batch_compute.py::test_library_and_mcp_shape
```

All five raise `RebarError: Error: ticket system not initialized` from `_reads.py` — the new
guard.

`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.materialize_tickets` materializes the pinned ticket store as a **bare
tree**: a throwaway index + `git checkout-index --prefix=` into
`<store>/tickets-<sha>/.tickets-tracker/`, then an atomic rename. There is no `git init`
anywhere on that path. The result is a fully valid, deliberately read-only ticket store **with
no `.git` at all** — and the gates point their rebar ticket tools straight at it
(`config.tracker_dir(<root>)`).

Materialized store from the failing run, dumped directly:

```
DIR: …/rebar-gate-snapshots/tickets-07ecc09ddfad…/.tickets-tracker
  .bridge_state  .gitattributes  .gitignore  .pre-commit-config.yaml
  .store-compat.json  2f02-a8a0-942c-4d35     <-- a real ticket
  .git present? NO
```

So a `.git`-less tracker directory holding ticket data is exactly the shape of BOTH:

- the **poisoned production volume** this bug is about (marker files, no `.git`), and
- a **legitimate, current, pinned gate snapshot** that must read normally.

`.git`-presence cannot separate them. The approved predicate rejects both, which means every
gate read of a pinned ticket snapshot — plan-review and completion-verifier, the two op-cert
kinds — starts raising `store_uninitialized`. That is a P1-class regression introduced by a P1
fix, and neither session's targeted regression tests cover the shape, because both fixtures
build only *broken* `.git`-less stores.

**This is the "the plan is wrong, say so with evidence" case, so I am escalating rather than
redesigning.** For the record, the shape of a predicate that could work: discriminate on
whether the directory *is a well-formed ticket store* (the layout the reducer needs —
e.g. `.store-compat.json` plus event dirs), and apply the git/HEAD usability probe only as an
ADDITIONAL condition *when `.git` is present* (which still catches the mid-clone case, since a
clone in flight has `.git` with an unresolvable HEAD). The poisoned production volume, which
held only `reviewbot-ensure-tickets` marker files and no ticket data, fails a
well-formedness test; the gate snapshot passes it. But that is a different predicate from the
approved one and needs a fresh plan-review, not an in-flight substitution.

### CAUSE 2 (implementation) — the probe violates the lock-held-git timeout invariant

```
tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py::test_stage_and_commit_git_calls_are_all_timeout_bounded
AssertionError: a lock-held git call ran without a timeout: [None, 30, 30]
```

`store_is_usable` calls `subprocess.run` with no `timeout=`. Because the predicate is now
shared with `event_prepare._ensure_initialized`, that unbounded call runs **inside the store's
MKDIR write lock**. Ticket `c2ba-98bf-ca2d-481a` established the invariant that every
lock-held git call is wall-clock bounded, precisely so a stuck or contended tracker volume
cannot hold the write lock indefinitely — the residue behind the autodeploy incident recorded
there. The approved plan's pre-mortem considered a missing git binary but not a HANGING one.

This half is straightforwardly fixable — bound the probe with the same `_GIT_TIMEOUT`
`push.py`/`event_append.py` use, and decide explicitly whether a timeout means "not usable"
or is a distinct fault like the `OSError` case. It should be an acceptance criterion either
way, since nothing in the current plan pins it.

### Status of my branch

`9ebaa3490e48` on `aefe-store-usability` (off `origin/main` `565e1856`). **Not pushed** — it
is a duplicate of `84237944cedb` and, more importantly, it should not land in this form. My
targeted regression file is 30/30 green and mutation-clean (6/6 killed), `make lint` and
`make typecheck` both rc=0, complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0` — the change does exactly
what the plan approved. The plan is what needs revisiting.

## Final report — /rebar-debug Phase 2 landed for review (Option A)

**Gerrit change:** https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2365 (commit `902f027a3d5c`,
`rebar-ticket:` trailer + DCO). Plan-review **PASS / certified** at head `902f027a`
(`verified_at_sha` 483477df, currency_basis file_impact). Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`
before Submit; ticket stays `in_progress` until merged.

**Problem.** `_reads._tracker` gated reads on `os.path.isdir(tracker)` only, so a directory that
exists but is not a usable store returned `[]` instead of raising `store_uninitialized` — a broken
store indistinguishable from an empty one.

**Proven root cause (RCA in prior comment).** `_reads._tracker()` (`src/rebar/_reads.py`) fires the
guard only when the dir is ABSENT; a present-but-unusable tracker (marker files, no `.git`, or
`.git` with unresolvable HEAD) satisfies `isdir`, so every library/MCP read reduced to `[]`.
Attributed to `44fd-230c-5893-4246` (commit `84fc5f9b`).

**Final predicate (operator-approved Option A — one shared content-based seam).**
`store_usability.store_is_usable(tracker)` = `isdir` AND EITHER
1. `.git` present AND `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves (via the store's bounded runner), OR
2. carries store STRUCTURE — a committed `.store-compat.json` record, OR ≥1 non-dot event dir
   (legacy fallback, mirrors `reducer/_api.py`).

Both `_reads._tracker` and the write guard `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` call this ONE
predicate — no mode flag, no second path — so read and write cannot diverge.

**Three-case matrix (all test-pinned, GREEN):**
| Case | Fixtures | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Production incident — marker files only, no `.git`/`.store-compat.json`/event dirs | `_tracker_present_without_git` | **RAISES `store_uninitialized`** ✅ |
| Empty-but-initialized LIVE store — `.git` + resolvable HEAD | `_initialized_empty_repo` | reads `[]` ✅ |
| Materialized snapshot — `.git`-LESS, committed `.store-compat.json` + event dir | `_gitless_snapshot_repo` | **READS** ✅ (gate-agent regression fix) |

**Empty-snapshot edge (operator ruling):** a `.git`-less snapshot with `.store-compat.json` and
ZERO events is VALID via the committed marker → reads `[]`
(`test_empty_materialized_snapshot_reads_empty`). The predicate is never keyed on emptiness.

**Write-path timeout fix.** The HEAD probe reuses `gitutil.run_git_bounded(tracker, "rev-parse",
"--verify", "-q", "HEAD", timeout=...)` — the store's existing bounded runner (folds
`TimeoutExpired`→rc 124; `OSError` propagates). No unbounded git call enters the write path;
`test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba::test_stage_and_commit_git_calls_are_all_timeout_bounded` GREEN.

**Test (RED→GREEN, held out from the fix, mutation-checked).**
`tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`. New: `test_materialized_snapshot_reads_instead_of_raising`,
`test_empty_materialized_snapshot_reads_empty`, and the seeded-mutation guard
`test_store_structure_clause_is_load_bearing_for_snapshot_reads` (strip clause 2 → snapshot read
returns to RAISE), plus the extended `store_is_usable` predicate matrix. Mutation seam exercised via
`monkeypatch` of `_carries_store_structure`.

**Caller-sweep re-verification (against the NEW predicate).** Broad run
`pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces -n auto` = **16419 passed**. The 6 previously-red tests are now
GREEN: `test_gate_ticket_snapshot` ×4, `test_next_batch_compute::test_library_and_mcp_shape`,
`test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba`. All 7 `_tracker` entry points + the `.git`-less snapshot path
behave correctly; the sole `store_uninitialized` consumer (`audit.server._audited_tickets`)
degrades safely and now logs.

**Scope & safety.** Restores read/write parity (no new capability, no new dependency); no existing
test weakened (only `test_reads_uninitialized_store.py` touched among tests). `make lint`
(complexity ratchet new=0/increased=0) + `make typecheck` PASS.

**Pre-existing environmental failures (NOT mine, do not fix).** 8 sandbox-git topology failures —
`test_atomic_completion_close.py` ×5, `test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated`,
`test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` ×2 — all fail with `git … show-ref/ls-tree refs/heads/tickets`
→ exit 128 on clean `origin/main`; none is in this diff. Separately, one load-only flake surfaced
under `-n auto` (`test_wiki_render_hardening.py::test_a_timeout_reaps_the_whole_process_group_not_just_the_child`)
but passes 3/3 in isolation and is unrelated to store usability.

**Siblings (Step 7 parity).** CLI read path (`reads_cli.py`) and other bare-`isdir` read sites →
`free-slothful-fennecfox` (be80-8377-4b4c-44f4), `discovered_from` this ticket.

**Replication.** The original report (a present-but-unusable tracker read returning `[]`) no longer
reproduces: `rebar.list_tickets` on a marker-file-only dir now raises `store_uninitialized`
(production-incident AC, GREEN).

Close will carry `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=44fd-230c-5893-4246` once the change is
`Verified +1` and merged.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`_reads._tracker` raises `store_uninitialized` only when the tracker directory is ABSENT
(`src/rebar/_reads.py`, `if not os.path.isdir(tracker)`). A directory that EXISTS but is not a
usable store — no `.git`, or a `.git` with no resolvable HEAD, or one mid-clone — satisfies
`isdir`, so every read returns `[]`. A broken store is indistinguishable from an empty one, the
exact confusion the guard was added to remove. Hit three times: the deployed MCP server served an
empty tracker (marker files, no `.git`); `fathomable-yester-thrip` change 2244 residual; and
`unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` AC3. Full RCA and escalation are in prior comments.

## Constraints

- An existing, empty, INITIALIZED store must still read `[]` — a real contract with an existing
  test. The discriminator cannot be emptiness.
- `.env-id` is ruled out as the predicate (git-ignored, absent right after a valid clone).
- A `.git`-LESS materialized ticket snapshot must READ: `_snapshot.materialize_tickets` checks the
  committed tickets tree out into a `.git`-less `.tickets-tracker/`, and the code-review gate
  agents read it in production. A `.git`+HEAD-only predicate breaks that surface (the escalation
  the operator resolved with Option A).

## Fix (operator-approved Option A — one shared content-based seam)

New stdlib-only leaf `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py::store_is_usable(tracker)`: usable when
`isdir` AND EITHER (1) `.git` present with a resolvable HEAD (`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`), OR
(2) it carries the store STRUCTURE — a committed `.store-compat.json` record (survives the snapshot
checkout, present even in a zero-event store), or ≥1 non-dot event dir (legacy fallback, mirrors
`reducer/_api.py` enumeration). `_reads._tracker` calls `store_is_usable` directly; the write guard
`event_prepare._ensure_initialized` calls `store_is_writable` = `store_is_usable` AND `.git` present
(the write's inherent precondition — it commits events). Both flow through the ONE shared usability
predicate — no mode flag, no second path — so read and write cannot diverge on what an initialized
store is, while a `.git`-less read-only snapshot stays READABLE but correctly non-writable. Clause 2
keeps the `.git`-less snapshot readable while the
marker-file-only production incident still RAISES. Zero events + committed marker is VALID (reads
`[]`); the predicate is never keyed on emptiness.

The HEAD probe reuses the store's bounded runner `gitutil.run_git_bounded` (folds `TimeoutExpired`
to rc 124), so no unbounded git call enters the write path; a missing `git` binary (`OSError`)
propagates as a distinct environment fault, not `store_uninitialized`. The write gate does NOT
loosen: `_ensure_initialized` gates on `store_is_writable(tracker)` = `store_is_usable(tracker)`
AND `.git` present. It shares the usability predicate (so read and write agree on what an
initialized store IS) and then adds the write's inherent precondition — a write COMMITS events, so
it needs a real `.git` repository. This preserves the original `.git`-requiring write gate exactly:
a `.git`-less STRUCTURE-only snapshot is READABLE but NOT writable, and a mid-clone (`.git`, no
HEAD, no structure) is rejected by `store_is_usable` itself. One usability seam, no bypass flag.

The sole `store_uninitialized` consumer, the read-only audit web index
(`audit.server._audited_tickets`), still degrades a broken store to an empty page (must not 500)
but now LOGS a warning and its docstring no longer claims such a store is never blanked — behavior
unchanged; that promise held only while broken stores read `[]`. Caller sweep re-verified against
the NEW predicate: all 7 `_tracker` entry points and the `.git`-less snapshot path behave
correctly. Files: `store_usability.py` (new), `_reads.py`, `event_prepare.py`, `audit/server.py`,
`tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] READ: a dir with marker files only (no `.git`/`.store-compat.json`/event dirs) raises
      `store_uninitialized`, not `[]` — the production incident.
- [ ] READ: a mid-clone store (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable, no structure) raises
      `store_uninitialized`.
- [ ] READ: an existing empty INITIALIZED store (`.git`+HEAD) still reads `[]` (contract test
      unchanged).
- [ ] READ: a valid clone with resolvable HEAD but no `.env-id` still reads (reads differ from
      writes on `.env-id`).
- [ ] READ regression: a `.git`-LESS materialized snapshot with committed `.store-compat.json` +
      an event dir READS the ticket, not raises (the gate-agent path).
- [ ] READ edge: a `.git`-less snapshot with `.store-compat.json` and ZERO events reads `[]`.
- [ ] WRITE: `_ensure_initialized` (via `store_is_writable`) rejects a mid-clone store, rejects a
      `.git`-LESS materialized snapshot (readable but not writable — no repo to commit into), and
      still accepts an initialized one.
- [ ] WRITE: every `stage_and_commit` git call incl. the new HEAD probe is timeout-BOUNDED
      (`test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba`).
- [ ] PREDICATE: `store_is_usable` is False for absent/no-`.git`/mid-clone/empty-dir and True for
      an initialized store, a HEAD-resolvable clone without `.env-id`, a snapshot, an
      event-dir-only legacy store, and an empty-but-committed snapshot.
- [ ] PREDICATE: a missing `git` binary (OSError) PROPAGATES rather than reporting
      `store_uninitialized` (T5b failure-taxonomy).
- [ ] AUDIT: `audit.server._audited_tickets` renders empty AND logs a warning for a
      present-but-unusable store.
- [ ] Mutation guard: stripping the store-structure clause returns the `.git`-less snapshot read
      to RAISING `store_uninitialized` (defect-seeded, sandboxed).

## Testing

RED→GREEN in `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`; run
`python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py -q` (all cases above green). Broad
re-verification: `python -m pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces -q -n auto` — the 6 previously-red
snapshot/next-batch/write-timeout tests are green; `make lint` (complexity ratchet
new=0/increased=0) and `make typecheck` pass. The pre-existing sandbox-git failures
(`show-ref`/`ls-tree refs/heads/tickets` → 128) fail identically on clean `origin/main` and are
environmental, not from this change.

Out of approved scope (parity — discovered ticket): CLI read path (`reads_cli.py`) and other
bare-`isdir` read sites → `free-slothful-fennecfox` (be80-8377-4b4c-44f4).

file_impact.reason: new stdlib-only leaf: shared content-based store_is_usable predicate = isdir AND ((.git present AND HEAD resolves via bounded gitutil.run_git_bounded) OR carries store structure: committed .store-compat.json OR >=1 well-formed ticket event dir holding an event .json). Accepts .git-less materialized snapshots; rejects marker-file-only production incident and stray non-event subdirs. HEAD probe timeout-bounded (write-path safe); OSError propagates
read chokepoint _tracker raises store_uninitialized when store not usable, across all 7 library/MCP read entry points; .git-less snapshot with store structure still reads

write guard _ensure_initialized shares the predicate; clause 2 does not loosen the write gate (a mid-clone live store carries no well-formed event dir and no committed record); mid-clone still rejected
reconcile the sole store_uninitialized consumer: correct docstring + broaden warning log so a present-but-unusable store is logged not silently blanked (behavior unchanged: index still renders empty)

document the agent-visible read-contract widening: reads now error store_uninitialized on a present-but-unusable store (not only absent), .git-less materialized snapshots still read, one shared read+write usability predicate

regression: production-incident/mid-clone/stray-subdir READ raise; empty-init and no-env-id clone read; .git-less materialized snapshot (compat+event dir) READS; empty-snapshot reads []; write-gate mid-clone rejected + timeout-bounded; git-missing OSError propagates; audit renders-empty+logs; store_is_usable predicate matrix; store-structure-clause mutation guard
